failure_analysis.what_failed: The fixed-recipe supervisor ignores disturbances, so when a feed draw, pump-gain loss, or split shift raises the pump voltage needed to hold h1, v2 saturates at 12 V and h3 exceeds 0.75 m for hundreds of seconds. Production also drifts during oscillations because the loops cannot compensate without moving the setpoint split.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the open-loop recipe with a model-based supervisor that estimates effective pump gains and feed disturbances from the differential mass balances, then searches the constant-production setpoint curve for the point that keeps predicted upper levels below margin and pump voltages away from saturation while minimising setpoint travel.

self_check: The supervisor uses derivative-corrected mass balances to estimate effective pump gains and unmeasured feed flows every call, so it distinguishes a real disturbance from its own transient. It then searches the Q=target setpoint curve for the pair that keeps predicted h3 and h4 below a 0.72 m margin and both voltages inside 1.0-11.6 V, preferring the smallest setpoint movement. If no feasible pair exists, it minimises predicted upper-level and voltage violations, which prevents v2 from saturating and h3 from running away.
proposed_change: Add a model-based supervisor that estimates k1e, k2e, d1, d2 online from the mass-balance derivatives and selects the minimum-travel setpoint pair on the target-production curve that keeps predicted h3/h4 below 0.72 m and pump voltages within 1.0-11.6 V.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The fixed recipe never moves the setpoints, so it has no way to use the free degree of freedom. When tank1 loses liquid (feed draw-off d1<0), the off-diagonal h1 loop drives pump 2 (v2) to its 12 V saturation, which pushes h3 far above the 0.75 m upper-level limit and also droops production because the loop can no longer hold h1. The same saturation logic lets combined and pump-sine disturbances push h3/h4 over the limit and h2 out of band, while target changes are met only by re-scaling both setpoints.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Estimate the effective per-volt gains and additive disturbances online from the window, compute the steady-state (h1,h2) pairs that satisfy a target production Q and all level/voltage constraints, and pick the feasible pair with minimum setpoint travel; cap v2 (hence h3) and v1 (hence h4) from the measured upper-tank relations.

self_check: The code measures the current upper tank levels and voltages, converts them to effective per-volt flows and to the h3/h4 limits, so it knows the exact pump-voltage ceilings that keep both upper tanks below the limit. It then solves the linear steady-state balances for the pump voltages required by any candidate (h1,h2) split of the target production and only accepts splits whose voltages stay inside those ceilings, inside 1-12 V, inside the h2 band and the h1/h2 safety limits. Among the feasible splits it returns the one closest to the currently active setpoints, and it holds the setpoints whenever the active point is already feasible, so production stays on target with the least travel. When no split can hold every constraint, it chooses the closest achievable production so that a small production shortfall replaces an expensive, sustained level violation.
proposed_change: Replace the fixed scaled recipe with an online estimator (effective valve/pump gains and additive feed offsets from the window, with a slope correction and oscillation guard) plus a steady-state feasibility solve: intersect the q1-interval implied by the v1/v2 ceilings (from the measured h3/h4 limits), the h2 band and the h1/h2 safety limits, and pick the minimum-travel feasible setpoint pair for the (clamped) production target.
reason: 'nominal' disturbances got worse on average: 251.8 -> 423.4, allowed +63

failure_analysis.what_failed: The fixed scaled recipe ignores disturbances, so when a tank1 draw (or gamma/valve shift) forces the h1 loop to raise pump2, tank3 level climbs past 0.75 m while pump2 saturates at 12 V; hundreds of seconds of upper-level violation dominate the score. Symmetrically, tank2-side disturbances push tank4 up. The supervisor never touches setpoints (travel 0), so it cannot use the free production-split degree of freedom.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Use a steady-state model of the four-tank balances to estimate the disturbance from the measured upper-level flows, then pick the tank1/tank2 production split (on the constant-Q curve) that keeps h3, h4 and the pump voltages safely inside limits; re-evaluate every call with a short hold after our own setpoint moves.

self_check: The supervisor estimates the unmeasured load from the measured inflows to tank3/tank4 (a3*sqrt(2gh3), a4*sqrt(2gh4)), solves the two lower-tank balances for the pump flows A,B, and predicts h3, h4, v1, v2 for every candidate split on the constant-production curve q1+q2=Q. If h3 or the pump2 voltage is predicted to exceed its margin, it lowers the h1 setpoint and raises h2 (shifting production toward tank2), and it does the mirror move if h4 or v1 is the binding constraint; the h2 band and setpoint/safety limits are enforced as hard bounds. Because Q is fixed by the chosen curve, production stays on target while the split absorbs the disturbance. A short hold after our own setpoint change prevents reacting to the loop's settling transient.
proposed_change: Replace the blind scaled recipe with a model-based split selector: estimate the load from the upper-level flows, then grid-search the tank1/tank2 split that minimizes predicted upper-level, band and saturation penalties plus a small setpoint-travel cost. Return those setpoints, holding steady for a short window after our own change to avoid chasing transients.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor over-reacts to oscillatory (sine) feed/pump/split disturbances: it recomputes d1,d2,k1e,k2e from single, transient-contaminated samples, so the estimates swing sign and it drives large setpoint runs (up to 1.1 m travel). Those swings keep the base PI loops permanently in transient, so production never settles (e.g. 758 L off target in dev_feed_sine_2), and the mis-timed shifts push h2 below/above its band and h3 over the 0.75 m limit (dev_feed_sine_2, dev_feed_sine_1, dev_combined_sine_1, dev_pump_sine_0).
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the single-sample disturbance estimate with a robust average over recent quasi-steady, non-saturated samples, and only move setpoints when the predicted steady state at the current operating point actually violates a constraint; dead-band and rate-limit the moves.

self_check: The supervisor estimates slowly-varying load (d1,d2) and pump-gain losses (k1e,k2e) only from recent samples that are quasi-steady and have non-saturated pumps, then averages them, so a sinusoidal disturbance no longer produces oscillating setpoint commands. It holds the current setpoints whenever the predicted steady state at that operating point keeps h3,h4, v1,v2 and the h2 band within margin, and only shifts production along the constant-Q curve when a predicted upper level, pump voltage, or h2 actually breaches its limit. Moves are dead-banded and rate-limited so they settle instead of chattering, and the step is enlarged only while a real limit is being exceeded or the production target just changed.
proposed_change: Estimate effective disturbances/gains from a robust average of recent quasi-steady, unsaturated samples, and hold unless the model predicts a real constraint breach. Keep the constant-Q curve solve but add a feasibility dead-band, a rate limit, and a filtered load estimate so oscillatory disturbances no longer cause large setpoint swings.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The worst scores are all sinusoidal/combined disturbances and the pure target changes. The old supervisor estimated d1, d2 and the effective pump gains from the *steady-state residual* of the last sample only. Whenever the levels are still responding to its own setpoint move, or to a sine disturbance, that residual is badly biased (e.g. at t=250 s in dev_feed_sine_2 the true d2 is 1.75 L/s but the residual estimator reports 0.5 L/s). It therefore kept chasing with wrong, large setpoint moves (0.8-1.1 m travel), the 45 s post-move hold blocked corrections, and the plant was pushed until v1 saturated, h2 left [0.25,0.45] and h3 exceeded 0.75 m. Nominal target changes also over-travelled (0.15-0.30 m instead of ~0.074 m) because the L1-minimum-travel point on the constant-Q curve was not the one selected.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Estimate the additive feed offsets d1,d2 and the effective upper-tank gains exactly from the tank mass balances (using level derivatives) so the estimate is valid during setpoint transients and sine disturbances, delete the 45 s hold, and select the setpoint pair that minimises L1 setpoint travel on the constant-production curve subject to margined h2/h3/h4 and pump-voltage limits.

self_check: The supervisor converts the measured levels into the exact feed offsets d1,d2 and pump gains via the tank mass balances (level slopes), so a candidate setpoint's required pump voltages and upper levels are predicted correctly even while the loops are still settling. It then picks the point on the constant-production curve that is closest in L1 setpoint travel while keeping h2 inside a margined band, h3/h4 below a margined ceiling and v1/v2 inside a margined voltage window; if an upper level approaches its limit the solver automatically moves production to the other tank (which lowers the offending upper level), and if a pump approaches saturation it moves along the curve in the direction that reduces that pump's required voltage rather than dropping the production target. The move is rate-limited along the curve so the commanded pair never leaves the target-production curve, and a small deadband suppresses travel from estimator noise.
proposed_change: Replace the steady-state residual estimator with an exact mass-balance (level-derivative) estimator of d1, d2 and the effective upper-tank pump gains, remove the 45 s post-setpoint-change hold, and return the minimum-L1-travel setpoint pair on the constant-production curve that satisfies margined h2-band, h3/h4 and pump-voltage limits. This keeps Q on target while adapting production split only as far as the constraints require.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor estimated the unmeasured feeds from steady-state upper-level flows (f3,f4 treated as the pump flows), but tank3/tank4 have ~2-3 min time constants, so during fast feed/split oscillations the estimate lagged and mis-signed the required action. It then chased the resulting transient: e.g. a positive tank2 feed lowers pump1 flow, starves tank1, makes the h1 loop raise pump2 and push h3 up, yet the supervisor shifted production toward tank2 (raising the h2 setpoint), worsening h2 band excursions and driving v2 into saturation (>12 V), producing large production off-target and h3 above 0.75 m. Because it recomputed every call it also oscillated, adding setpoint travel.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: On oscillatory feed/split disturbances, low-pass the disturbance estimate and keep setpoints steadier; verify that transient pump overshoot (~1.5 V) is covered by the voltage margin used in the steady-state prediction so upper levels are not chased during loop transients.

self_check: The supervisor estimates the two unmeasured feeds from an exact finite-difference mass balance that keeps the upper-tank storage terms (dh3/dt, dh4/dt), then averages them over ~70 s so fast oscillations do not move the setpoints, and searches the constant-production curve for the split that keeps predicted h3/h4 below the limit and pump voltages inside 1-12 V, choosing the point closest to the current setpoints. When a disturbance drives h3 or h4 toward the limit, the required pump flows A and B are recomputed and production is shifted off the loading tank along the constant-Q curve, which lowers the corresponding pump voltage and upper level. If a pump nears saturation the voltage term in the cost pulls the setpoint back so the loop stops demanding more than 12 V, trading a small production error for avoiding limit violations. Rate limiting to 0.06 m per call plus a deadband keeps setpoint travel small so the PI loops are not re-excited.
proposed_change: Replace the steady-state flow-through-pump disturbance estimate with an exact finite-difference mass-balance residual (including upper-tank storage) that is low-passed to reject fast oscillations, estimate effective pump gains, and pick the minimum-travel split on the constant-production curve using transient safety margins on h3/h4 and pump voltages. Add a deadband, a rate limit, and a short hold so the supervisor stops chasing its own loop transients.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The steady-state mass-balance load estimate (d1,d2) is only correct when the plant is settled at the active setpoints. During sinusoidal feed/combined disturbances it swings out of phase with the true load, so the supervisor chases it: it swings sp_h2 between ~0.24 and ~0.40, driving h2 below the 0.25 band edge and pushing h3 above 0.75, while v1 pins at 12 V so Q falls ~1 L/s off target and setpoint travel grows to >1 m.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: If residual h2-band exits remain during sines, replace the symmetric err2 margin with a phase-aware tracking-error estimate (compare h2-sp_h2 over the rising vs falling load half-cycle) and bias sp_h2 accordingly.

self_check: The supervisor never returns an h2 setpoint outside the band margins, and it charges the split cost for the worst-case h2 that the loops can reach (setpoint +/- the measured h2 tracking error), so a disturbance cannot drag h2 out of the band just because the prediction is optimistic. When the load estimate oscillates, the code keeps its fast phase-lagged value out of the decision and instead evaluates each candidate split under both the low and high observed load, so h3 stays under the upper-level target and v1/v2 stay under an 11.4 V margin; if the two extremes conflict it picks the split that minimizes the combined margin violations, which automatically biases production away from the pump that is saturating. Effective pump gains are re-estimated from the measured upper-tank flows, so a 30% gain loss translates into a higher predicted voltage and the split shifts off that pump before it saturates. Consecutive commands are rate-limited and dead-banded, so oscillation does not produce setpoint travel.
proposed_change: Estimate d1/d2 only from windows of quasi-steady samples, and when those estimates oscillate use the window mean plus its observed range as two load scenarios instead of chasing the instantaneous value. Add an h2 setpoint margin equal to the observed h2 tracking error, enforce an upper-level margin in the split cost, and re-estimate effective pump gains so the free degree of freedom is spent only when a constraint is genuinely threatened.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor estimates the feed disturbance from the single latest sample, so for oscillatory (sine) feed disturbances its setpoint command lags the oscillation in phase. It then chases the reversing disturbance, swinging the setpoints (travel up to 1.1 m), which forces the PI loops to slew and makes production Q swing by up to +/-1.3 L/s; the large h1 commands also drive pump 2 hard and push h3 over its limit, and the over-commands saturate pump 1 and drop h2 below its band. Instantaneous-step scenarios are handled well, so only the oscillatory cases collapse.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Decouple the command from the instantaneous residual: derive the setpoint split from a windowed statistic of the disturbance (extreme-hold where a hard upper-level constraint binds, mean where the danger is soft pump saturation) so periodic disturbances yield a near-constant split while steps and ramps still bias it, and keep the constrained constant-production-curve solve with pump-saturation and level margins.

self_check: The split is solved on the constant-production curve using a windowed draw estimate: the window minimum of the tank1 feed residual pre-biases the split toward tank2 for as long as a draw is present, so an oscillating draw yields a fixed (not chasing) setpoint and tank3 stays below its limit, while the window mean of the tank2 residual removes zero-mean oscillation and only responds to sustained offsets. Within the solve I penalise any candidate split whose predicted h3/h4 exceed the limit, whose h2 leaves the band, or whose required pump voltages leave [1,12] V, using effective pump gains estimated from recent data, so a saturating or gain-degraded pump causes the supervisor to shift production to the other tank instead of demanding an unreachable level. Setpoint motion is rate-limited and biased to minimum travel so the loops are not excited; if the disturbance is genuinely infeasible the solver returns the least-cost split rather than oscillating.
proposed_change: Replace the single-sample disturbance residual with windowed statistics: the minimum of the tank1 feed residual (robust to oscillation, reacts immediately to a step-draw) and the mean of the tank2 feed residual over the last ~150 samples. Keep the constant-production-curve constrained solve with h3/h4/h2 margins and pump-voltage limits, using effective pump gains from recent samples.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The two worst scenarios are the oscillatory feed/combined sines plus the nominal target changes. On the sines the supervisor chases the disturbance with large, frequent, rate-limited setpoint moves; because its effective-gain estimate k1e=Am/v1 is taken from a transient upper-tank level, it underestimates the gain, decides pump 1 is near saturation, and pushes h1 far up, which drives predicted and actual h3 over the 0.75 m limit and saturates pump 1 (h2 droop + big production error). On nominal target changes the 0.06 m step clamp plus the 45 s 'hold after own change' ramp the setpoints toward the new constant-Q point over roughly 250 s, so production stays off target for the whole ramp.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the supervisor passive unless an objective actually needs action: hold the current setpoints whenever the model predicts production on target and h2/h3/h4 inside their margins, move decisively (no rate limit) when production is predicted off target or a scored limit is predicted breached, and estimate pump gains only from quasi-steady upper-tank samples so a scheduled split change is not mistaken for pump saturation.

self_check: The supervisor evaluates the steady state on the constant-production curve for every candidate h1/h2 split, explicitly re-solving the balance when pump 1 or pump 2 would saturate, so it can see the achieved h2 and production rather than the commanded ones. It only moves when production is predicted off target or h2/h3/h4 are predicted or measured to breach their margins, so an oscillation that stays feasible is not chased and production stays on target. Target changes are handled in one decisive move with no rate limit, so production reconverges within a single loop settling time. When a pump approaches saturation the predictor clamps its flow, recomputes the achieved split, and the cost search then biases production toward the other tank to restore Q and keep h2 in band.
proposed_change: Replace the transient-steady-state residual and the 0.06 m/45 s actuation with a derivative-corrected mass-balance disturbance estimate, quasi-steady pump-gain estimates, and a minimal-intervention decision rule that holds feasible setpoints and otherwise jumps straight to the feasible constant-Q split (immediately for target changes).

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor chased oscillatory disturbances because it used the instantaneous mass-balance residual (last sample) for d1,d2 and pump gains. In sinusoidal feed and combined scenarios this caused rapid setpoint reversals, large production excursions, upper-level overflows (e.g. h3 > 0.75 in dev_feed_sine_2 and dev_combined_sine_1), and excessive setpoint travel. The 45 s hold after own changes further delayed corrective action.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Validate that the range-based feasibility check with Q-error penalty does not sacrifice production unnecessarily for step and ramp disturbances, and tune the violation penalties if needed.

self_check: The supervisor estimates the disturbance range from the mass-balance residuals over a long window, using the full min/max when the signal oscillates and a short recent window when it does not. For each candidate split it computes the worst-case upper levels and pump voltages over that range, so it chooses setpoints that keep h3/h4 below the limit and pumps below saturation even at the extremes. If no feasible setpoint exists, it allows a small production error because the penalty for persistent upper-level overflow is higher than the score lost from a brief off-target excursion.
proposed_change: Replace the single-sample disturbance and pump-gain estimates with window-based robust estimates, and search over the full (q1, q2) space with a cost that trades production error against constraint violations and setpoint travel. Use the full-window min/max for oscillatory disturbances to prevent setpoint chasing.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor chased instantaneous oscillatory load estimates, causing setpoint oscillation, h2 band violations, and upper-level overflow in sine feed scenarios.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the instantaneous load estimate with robust window min/max bounds and use a constraint-prioritized search over setpoints to avoid overreacting to zero-mean oscillations.

self_check: The new logic estimates the feed load from mass balance over the entire 10-minute window, then uses the min and max estimates to bound worst-case disturbances for h3 and h4. It searches setpoints on the constant-Q curve to keep predicted h3/h4 below their limits and pumps within voltage, while penalizing h2 band and safety violations. This prevents chasing oscillations, so an upper level near its limit or a saturating pump is handled by a steady, conservative split rather than a series of reactive setpoint moves.
proposed_change: Use window min/max of mass-balance load estimates to bound worst-case h3/h4 and pump voltages, and search h1/h2 to minimize constraint violations, production error, and setpoint travel.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor lags oscillatory feed/split disturbances. It estimates the load from the last sample's steady-state residual (no dh/dt term, so biased while levels move), and it only actuates every ~45 s in 0.06 m steps, so its setpoint trajectory trails the sine by roughly 100-150 s. During the troughs pump1 saturates at 12 V and h2 drops to ~0.20 m (band violation), while during the peaks pump2 saturates and drives h3 above 0.75 m (123 s of upper-level violation). The same staircase also delays pure target-change moves, inflating the production-error integral.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the constrained constant-Q solve, but feed it the exact mass-balance load (including level slopes) and the exact pump gains, refresh it every call with no post-change hold, and rate-limit generously (fast after a target change). Next, harden the load estimate against split-valve shifts, which currently alias into d1/d2.

self_check: The supervisor now estimates the plant load each call from the full total-mass balance, including the measured level slopes, so it sees the true disturbance even while the PI loops are still settling, and it re-solves the constrained constant-production split every 10 s instead of every 45 s. When a disturbance pushes h3 or h4 toward the limit, the cost function penalises the predicted upper level above ulim-0.04 m and shifts production toward the other tank along the constant-Q curve until the predicted level is back inside. When a pump nears 12 V, the same solve penalises predicted voltages above 11.4 V and moves the split away from the saturated pump, so the h2 band is held by the pump that still has headroom. Setpoints are rate-limited (faster only right after a target change) with a 4 mm deadband, keeping travel small.
proposed_change: Add the level-slope term to the mass-balance load estimate, recover the effective pump gains from the upper-tank balances, and solve the constrained constant-Q split every call with margins on upper levels and pump voltage, with a fast rate limit when the production target changes. Drop the 45 s post-change hold that was causing the phase lag.
